.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes to the forecast this evening. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Rain returns Thursday as colder temperatures follow Friday
  into the weekend, with mountain snow and brisk conditions.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Rain returns Thursday as colder temperatures 
follow Friday into the weekend, with mountain snow and brisk 
conditions.

Dry and warm conditions are going to continue through Wednesday as 
upper troughing pulls offshore and weak ridging quickly traverses 
the region. Another chilly night ahead as skies remain clear and 
winds are calm across most of the area. Lows tonight settle in the 
mid 30s to lower 40s. A bit more cloud cover tomorrow keeps highs in 
the mid to upper 60s, but that is still above normal for this time 
of year. 

A low pressure system passing through the Ohio River Valley and into 
the Mid-Atlantic brings scattered showers across our region beginning 
Thursday morning across the Alleghenies. Showers are expected to 
move eastward across the area throughout the day. Depending on how 
fast this system moves offshore, precipitation could linger into 
Friday although primarily confined to the Allegheny Mountains and 
east of I-95.

The upper trough across the Northeast to OH Valley to Mid-Atlantic 
cuts off Friday, meanders south a bit on Saturday, then quickly 
flattens out Sunday into early next week as strong Canadian High 
pressure builds in from the west. Behind Thursday's cold front, 
temperatures are forecasted to be 5-10 degrees below mid November 
normals. Reinforcing fronts are likely to cross the area through the 
weekend, maintaining cold temperatures and brisk winds. Combined 
with ample cloud cover this brings us the season's first noticeable 
cold period.

The Allegheny Mountains are likely see their first accumulating snow 
of the season Friday into Saturday. A deepening low off the southern 
coast of New England will produce northwest winds into the 
mountains, with moisture feeding in a favorable direction from the 
Great Lakes. As temperatures cool Thursday night, rain transitions 
to a rain/snow mix, then likely all snow sometime on Friday. 
Marginal temperatures on Friday prevent much of that from 
accumulating, but that should change Friday night as temps drop to 
the 20s in the Alleghenies. Elevations above 3000 feet are most 
likely to see accumulating snow, but the marginal temps during the 
daytime should keep snow totals on the low end (at least compared to 
what some of the model guidance is indicating). As the surface high 
builds in on Sunday, drier air should bring an end to snow showers 
by Sunday afternoon.

Chilly and brisk conditions continue on Sunday as high pressure 
builds to our west. Winds calm next week with temperatures remaining 
below normal.

&&

.AVIATION /02Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
VFR conditions continue through Wednesday night. An area of low 
pressure will move across the OH Valley to Mid-Atlantic Thursday 
into Friday, then a strong upper trough brings brisk winds and cold 
conditions into the weekend. While some showers are expected 
Thursday, they likely won't cause significant restrictions. Some low 
clouds are possible Thursday into Thursday night. The cold front 
crosses the area Friday, then begins a period of brisk northwest 
winds gusting around 20-30 knots Friday into Saturday. While winds 
decrease a bit Sunday, the forecast still calls for gusts of 20-25 
knots.

&&

.MARINE...
Expect light winds tonight into Wednesday. An area of low 
pressure will move from the OH Valley to Mid-Atlantic Thursday 
into Friday, then a strong cold front moves across the area to 
start the weekend. A prolonged period of SCA conditions is 
likely to begin Thursday night and continue through Sunday 
afternoon. Most gusts are going to be around 20-25 knots, then 
gusts close to 30 knots are possible Friday into Friday night.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies are forecast to increase Wednesday into Thursday
as south winds return. Sensitive locations could approach Action
Stage, with Annapolis possibly reaching minor flood stage during
the Thursday afternoon high tide. After that, a strong cold
front brings a prolonged period of offshore winds. This could
result in blowout tides into the weekend.
